instruction.text: Read the way to stay safe while swimming. Select all the weather conditions mentioned.

atoms.a: When I swim outside, I should get out of the water immediately if there is lightning, thunder, heavy rain or fog.
atoms.b: When I swim outside, I should get out of the water immediately if there is ((lightning)), ((thunder)), ((heavy rain)) or ((fog)).

instruction.text: Which pictures show weather conditions you should not swim in?

feedback.end: These are all dangerous conditions for swimming. Thunderstorms can be life-threatening, and heavy rain or fog means the lifeguards won’t be able to see you.

instruction.text: Read the way to stay safe while swimming. Select all the floatation aids mentioned.

atoms.a: Arm bands, inflatable toys and lilos are not safe and do not protect me from drowning.
atoms.b: ((Arm bands)), ((inflatable toys)) and ((lilos)) are not safe and do not protect me from drowning.

instruction.text: Why are inflatables like lilos not safe?

b: ++The material of a lilo can easily break and lose air through barely visible holes.
A lilo cannot keep a person afloat.
Lilos can explode in cold water.

atoms.text: Markus can swim, but he still lacks the strength for long distances.
He likes to play in the sea near the beach on his lilo. However, there is an offshore wind today.
While he is lying down, he starts to be blown out to sea by the wind.
Now, he has realised he is very far out and unable to swim back in.

instruction.text: What does Markus need to do now?

feedback.end: Exactly! He will not be able to swim back, so he needs to call for help. This is why we should never use inflatables in the sea, and we should avoid using kayaks and stand up paddleboards in offshore winds.

b: ++Wave with both hands to the lifeguards.
Lie on the lilo and hope the wind changes.

instruction.text: Read the way to stay safe while swimming. Select all the words that describe water that is safe to jump into.
instruction.sound: Read the way to stay safe while swimming. Select all the words that describe water that is safe to jump in-to.

atoms.a: I only jump into the water where the water is deep and clear.
atoms.b: I only jump into the water where the water is ((deep)) and ((clear)).

instruction.text: Select the object that makes the situation dangerous.
Which pictures show places where you can safely jump into the water?

feedback.wrong1: There is a sign here prohibiting jumping into the water.
feedback.wrong2: Here it is difficult to see where the rocks are under the water surface.
feedback.finish: Great! We should only jump or dive where we know it’s safe.

instruction.text: What can you do to check whether a swimming spot is safe? Select all of the correct answers.

b: ++Be careful when entering the water for the first time.
++Before jumping, climb in and check how deep it is.
